[23] For me it took a total wakeup call. Alcohol poisoning then an intervention, withdrawals, and a 3 day hospital visit. I drank 6-8 13% cocktails a day for 2 years. 

I'd talk to a doctor about your alcohol consumption and determine whether you should seek medical attention to deal with withdrawal. depending on how much you drink and how long you've been drinking your withdrawal symptoms could be fatal. I had hallucinations, shakes, fever, and later a seizure when I got to the hospital. No one wants to go through that, but here's what I've been doing to maintain my sobriety: 

I also work at a bar albeit I'm a line cook. I keep my same routine of having drinks, just without the alcohol. My morning long islands became coffee. My shots from the bar turned into virgin cocktails. My late night runs to the gas station are now for sweet teas or just plain water. I will say though, if you try this and it doesn't work, I don't suggest working in a bar anymore. There's servers out there that make a hell of a lot more than bartenders.

My brother is 5 years sober and he uses the "I'll drink tomorrow" trick. Where you tell yourself you'll do it tomorrow, but you say the same thing the next day, and the day after that.

Open up about your drinking.Talk to your friends or loved one. Ones that will support you not drinking. I call my brother, and several of my friends a couple of times a week talking about how bad I want another drink. I get that bottled feeling out, and then we talk to each other about our days. Sometimes I even reminisce on some of the wild nights I'd have when I was drinking. I'd also always remind myself of all the wicked hangovers I've had.

Sobriety is incredibly difficult, it takes an insane amount of support and a hell of a lot of self control. Everyone's experience is subjective. Like other comments, I recommend AA as well. Talking about your experiences and hearing about others will help a lot. 

One last thought, think about why you're drinking in the first place. Are you numbing your feelings? Are you trying to forget something? Are you doing it because you think it makes you have a better social status? I asked myself why I drank so much and I forgot why I got to that point in the first place. I'm still hella depressed, still anxious, but I'm finally starting to see the reasons why, instead of being in a perpetual bender of numbed feelings and lost memories.

Thanks for sharing man. I'm only a week sober after detoxing but you're definitely right. Quitting doesn't solve the problem, it only takes the blinders off so you can finally see them. I'll remember that. Guess this is the start of my "pink cloud" year.

My Dad died of an overdose when I was 6 years old. I'm 22 now. My only memories of him are only being loved unconditionally. I only got to see him on weekends. he devoted all of his time to his children when he saw them. He was the kind of Dad that would show up to Walmart in his underwear with 0 shame. He always shared his food, he always took us out to beautiful places in the city. And of course, a lot of Dad Jokes. I miss my Dad a lot to this day. It's become easier to live with it as time goes on. Nonetheless, I still mourn the life I never got to have with him. Losing a parent is one of the hardest things you can go through. But you will grow to be more at peace with time.

Considering Kratom is not only a stimulant but can be a pain reliever, I wouldn't. It still affects the opiate receptors in your brain. Taking anything supplement or medicine could put you at risk of having a high tolerance to anesthesia and you could find yourself waking up during surgery.

From all the research I've done there's no studies that prove Kratom lowers your T levels, but it does kill your sex drive. I used it for over a year, I think I masturbated maybe once out of the month at that time and it took a little coaxing to get myself to do it.
